\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{امکان} \fa{پذیر} (emkân pazir)}{امکان پذیر (emkân pazir)}]{\fa{امکان} \fa{پذیر} (emkân pazir) — possible, feasible}

\label{lesson:FA-C398-emkan-pazir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to come up, then the Persian for an option.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{امکان} \fa{پذیر}}
\textbf{\fa{امکان} \fa{پذیر}} (\emph{emkân pazir}) — \textquotedblleft{}possible, feasible\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{این} \fa{طرح} \fa{با} \fa{این} \fa{پول} \fa{امکان} \fa{پذیر} \fa{نیست}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{in tarh bâ in pul emkân pazir nist.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This plan is not feasible with this money.
\end{quote}

\emph{Emkân} \textquotedblleft{}possibility\textquotedblright{} + \emph{pazir} \textquotedblleft{}accepting\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{paziroftan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{امکان} \fa{پذیر}} joins \emph{emkân} \textquotedblleft{}possibility\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Arabic \emph{imkān}, to \emph{pazir} \textquotedblleft{}accepting\textquotedblright{}, the present stem of the inherited verb \emph{paziroftan} (EtymDB traces it to Middle Persian): open to being possible.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{emkân pazir}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{emkân pazir}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{emkân pazir}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to come up, then the Persian for an option, then say \emph{emkân pazir} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{عملی} ('amali)}{عملی ('amali)}]{\fa{عملی} ('amali) — practical, workable}

\label{lesson:FA-C398-amali}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for an option, then the Persian for possible.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{عملی}}
\textbf{\fa{عملی}} (\emph{'amali}) — \textquotedblleft{}practical, workable\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پیشنهاد} \fa{تو} \fa{جالب} \fa{است،} \fa{اما} \fa{عملی} \fa{نیست}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pishnahâd-e to jâleb ast, ammâ 'amali nist.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Your suggestion is interesting, but it is not practical.
\end{quote}

\emph{'Amal} \textquotedblleft{}action, deed\textquotedblright{} + \emph{-i}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{عملی}} is built on \emph{'amal} \textquotedblleft{}deed, action\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Arabic \emph{'amal}, with the adjective suffix \emph{-i}: something that can be done.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بودجه} (budje)}{بودجه (budje)}]{\fa{بودجه} (budje) — a budget}

\label{lesson:FA-C398-budje}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for possible, then the Persian for practical.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بودجه}}
\textbf{\fa{بودجه}} (\emph{budje}) — \textquotedblleft{}a budget\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بودجه} \fa{این} \fa{پروژه} \fa{تمام} \fa{شده} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{budje-ye in prozhe tamâm shode ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The budget for this project has run out.
\end{quote}

A European loan. Plural \emph{budjehâ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{بودجه}} is a modern loan, usually traced to French \emph{budget}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اولویت} (owlaviyat)}{اولویت (owlaviyat)}]{\fa{اولویت} (owlaviyat) — a priority}

\label{lesson:FA-C398-owlaviyyat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for practical, then the Persian for a budget.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اولویت}}
\textbf{\fa{اولویت}} (\emph{owlaviyat}) — \textquotedblleft{}a priority\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{سلامت} \fa{بچه} \fa{ها} \fa{اولویت} \fa{اول} \fa{ماست}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{salâmat-e bachche hâ owlaviyat-e avval-e mâst.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The children's health is our first priority.
\end{quote}

Plural \emph{owlaviyathâ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{اولویت}} comes from Arabic \emph{awlawiyya} \textquotedblleft{}priority\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), which EtymDB derives from \emph{awlā} \textquotedblleft{}more deserving, nearer\textquotedblright{}.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{سنجیدن} (sanjidan)}{سنجیدن (sanjidan)}]{\fa{سنجیدن} (sanjidan) — to weigh up, to measure}

\label{lesson:FA-C398-sanjidan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a budget, then the Persian for a priority.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{سنجیدن}}
\textbf{\fa{سنجیدن}} (\emph{sanjidan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to weigh up, to measure\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{قبل} \fa{از} \fa{تصمیم} \fa{همه} \fa{گزینه} \fa{ها} \fa{را} \fa{سنجید}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{qabl az tasmim hame-ye gozine hâ râ sanjid.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Before deciding he weighed up all the options.
\end{quote}

Present stem \emph{sanj-}: \emph{misanjad}. Also to weigh on scales.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{سنجیدن}} is an inherited Persian verb \textquotedblleft{}to weigh, to measure\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Middle Persian; EtymDB lists it without a parent.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
